canonical_claim: The relink answer path must call `ensureRefTableRecovered`, suppress `sweepStalePrecommitsForRead` and `maybeScheduleSnapshotPublish`, and share one `resolveRef` implementation through a `ReadMaintenance` parameter rather than a parallel resolver.; For a cold table, `ensureRefTableRecovered` is mandatory on the peer-answer path, while `sweepStalePrecommitsForRead` and `maybeScheduleSnapshotPublish` are discretionary background work that a peer read must not schedule.

Peer-initiated recovery is bounded by a per-recovery work cap over pages, replay, and elapsed deadline, plus a hard-coded process-wide concurrency limit of one or two recoveries; exceeding either returns `Unknown` and increments a dedicated counter.; Removing the cold/evicted refusal trades the old zero-I/O property for boundedness: a peer may cause recovery work, but the work cap and process-wide concurrency limit bound it and an over-budget request returns `Unknown`.
`CasRefLedger::confirmExactRef` performs zero object-store I/O and reads only resident state; it never recovers, resolves a wedge, or materializes a runtime through `getRefTableRuntime`.

Held ref readers and lists must perform zero catalog GETs; a stale handle may see stale data or `NotFound`, but never a newer incarnation or a catalog-fence rejection caused solely by the hot read. Additionally, The ten `CasRefCatalog::read` sites in `CasRefLedger.cpp` were classified as admission/identity resolution, mutation authority, current-life destructive revalidation, held-handle hot path, or duplicate read; the file had zero held-handle-hot-path and zero duplicate-read removal sites. Additionally, The warm path of `acquireReadableRefTableRuntime` returns the resident runtime before any catalog read, so a held-runtime read issues zero catalog GETs unless separate maintenance work such as a stale-precommit sweep is armed. Additionally, The four read/list entry points `resolveRef`, `listRefs`, `hasAnyRefWithPrefix`, and `namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable` use `acquireReadableRefTableRuntime`; the warm held-runtime path reaches none of the ten catalog-read sites. Additionally, Once a ref runtime is warm and stale-precommit maintenance is disarmed, `resolveRef`, `listRefs`, and `hasAnyRefWithPrefix` issue zero requests against the catalog and no counted backend requests at all. Additionally, `confirmExactRef` and every observational `*ForTest` accessor use resident lookup only and perform no catalog or backend I/O, allocation, recovery, or runtime rebinding.; The ref-side read contract classifies catalog reads into admission/identity resolution, mutation authority, current-life destructive revalidation, held-handle hot path, and duplicate-read classes; only held-handle and duplicate reads are removal candidates.; `confirmExactRef` is a read-shaped API that performs zero object-store I/O and never materializes a ref-table runtime, so it reaches none of the ten `CasRefCatalog::read` sites classified in `CasRefLedger.cpp`.; The warm resident runtime path returns before either catalog read and therefore performs zero `ref_catalog` GETs.
Ref mutations may require an admission or authority catalog snapshot because mutations are not hot reads.

The required rebirth soak must include namespace-file readers and writers and prove zero reads resolve to a newer incarnation while dead-incarnation `_files` debris trends to zero through the janitor without blocking rebirth.
A stale held ref writer, if such an API exists, may write only to its old incarnation or fail and must never target a newer incarnation; no held ref-writer API should be invented solely for symmetry.

A `shadow/<bk>` directory on CA must be tombstone-aware: `existsDirectory` must enumerate namespaces with `listNamespaces` and consult tombstone-aware `listRefs`, because raw LIST counts tombstoned objects that have not yet been garbage-collected.

A stateless or ref-less reader is protected from GC with an ephemeral reader pin and a lost-replica timeout; the per-server-owned-namespace model narrows but does not eliminate the race window.; A stateless reader without a `/parts` reference needs an ephemeral Keeper pin in the MARK union so its parts cannot be swept during a SELECT.
Recovery after an ambiguous response must perform an exact `_ckpt` read and validate both the sampled token and the exact chain before installing.
Recovery closes the frontier by conditionally occupying the next slot with an in-band epoch seal; a late predecessor PUT is either adopted or fenced by that real object.
A decoded terminal seal in an epoch cannot authorize recovery past the same-epoch frontier.
The recovered owner set must use an `EpochSeal` as its checkpoint base rather than treating an arbitrary checkpoint as the owner-set base.

The CAS read path resolves refs through root-shard decode with TTL and single-flight caches, caches manifests by `(ManifestId, Token)`, performs one ranged S3 GET per column file per part open, and requests only files selected by `lookupPath`.

The CAS cache RFC scopes the proposed access layer to content-addressed metadata reads and committed part-reference mutations below `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`; it requires no `MergeTree` code changes.
All answers returned by `PartFolderView` are pure functions of that view.
The freshness modes are `CachedForLoad`, `ForceFreshMutable`, `FreshForWrite`, and `StrictValidate`.

`PartFolderView` caches semantic blob mappings but never blob payload bytes; missing or corrupt payload objects must still surface an exception.; The CA disk has no local byte cache; its read-path caches cover shard and manifest metadata only, so repeated blob reads refetch bytes from the object store.

`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` owns one `CachedPartFolderAccess` instance, and normal part/projection reads use it instead of repeated `resolveRouted` plus manifest lookup.; `CachedPartFolderAccess` is the only normal path for committed part-folder reads and committed part-reference mutations.; Every committed part/projection metadata operation that needs file or directory contents uses `getView` and answers from `PartFolderView`.
A cache-disabled `getView` does not retain the resulting `PartFolderView`, while lower-level CAS cache settings may remain independent until those caches move into `CasCacheState`.

The current CAS integration maps untyped disk-relative strings through PartPathParser and routing code to reconstruct table, part, projection, detached/shadow, and in-part file identity before reaching typed CAS objects.

A dedicated part storage cannot remove the generic path router because startup discovery, detached and shadow enumeration, table-level files, loose mountpoint objects, diagnostics, and direct IDisk clients still require a filesystem view.

The `allow_stale` read mode can return a cached shard value up to approximately 200 ms old, whereas force-fresh reads request the current value subject to backend consistency and writer-fencing limits.

After a same-name rebirth, a held readable runtime may return the old life's ref or no ref but must never return the successor life's ref; after the runtime is evicted and cold recovery runs, the same pool resolves the successor life.

The per-table snapshot-publish dispatch backoff starts at 1000 ms, doubles to 2000 ms, doubles again to a 4000 ms cap, and `resetPublishBackoff` clears the cooldown so a same-time over-threshold trigger dispatches immediately.

The private methods `admitSnapshotPublishUnderStateLock`, `advancePublishBackoff`, and `resetPublishBackoff` are characterized only through the public dispatch surface `appendRefOps` or `resolveRef` leading to `maybeScheduleSnapshotPublish`; their tests assert observable dispatch behavior rather than private return values.

Every caller of CasRefLedger::acquireReadableRefTableRuntime invokes ensureRefTableRecovered(ns, *rt) before reading state; resolveRef, listRefs, hasAnyRefWithPrefix, and namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable cannot expose an unrecovered cache, and a null runtime returns absence.
The allow_stale parameter of resolveRef is inert (bool /*allow_stale*/), so callers cannot request a stale reference read.
`Gc::enumerateRefPrefix` is retained after probe-A deletion and has exactly two callers: `Gc::listRefPrefix` and the `rebuildBaseline` rebuild path.

The converted test `CasRetirementSweep.TheRoundEnumeratesTheRefPrefixExactlyOnce` requires one `casRefsPrefix()` LIST per folding round and a positive count for the separate `namespaceRootPrefix()` janitor page. Additionally, `CasRetirementSweep.TheRoundEnumeratesTheRefPrefixExactlyOnce` classifies LIST calls by exact equality against `layout().casRefsPrefix()` (`cas/ns/stream/`) and `layout().namespaceRootPrefix()` (`cas/ns/`), so the janitor page cannot be counted as a hot ref-prefix scan. Additionally, The exactly-once enumeration anchor counts LIST calls for the whole ref prefix, not a total LIST budget: legitimate pagination would count greater than one, while replacing the full-prefix LIST with narrower per-namespace LISTs would not be detected.; `listRefPrefix` performs the single hot `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, reads the later catalog cut, constructs a capability-restricted `RoundInput`, and moves it immediately into the sole owning `RefPlan`.
